items.title: The closed subscheme cut out by the zeroth Fitting ideal agrees with the scheme theoretic support and carries the module
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma compares three closed subschemes attached to a finite type quasi-coherent module: the scheme theoretic support, the subscheme cut out by the zeroth Fitting ideal, and the support as a closed subset, and it adds that the module is pushed forward from the Fitting subscheme (statement lines 1309-1326). The counted proof is short but organises three separate points: the scheme theoretic inclusion from the elementary relation between the zeroth Fitting ideal and the annihilator, the equality of the underlying closed subsets from the corresponding property of Fitting ideals, and the existence of the required finite type module by pushing forward or by the closed subscheme/module equivalence (proof lines 1328-1349). It is H2: the argument is complete in the counted span and its inputs are the standard Fitting ideal and scheme theoretic support facts.
